description: Ecosistema IA para soluciones integrales de varios desafios a la vez
summary:
Project ACHE is a self-healing mesh of cooperating nodes that monitors its own
health in real time and reasons about trade-offs the way a crewed outpost on
the Moon or Mars would have to: balancing life support, power, shielding, and
connectivity under scarce resources. Each node runs independent probes that
measure RAM, disk, network coverage, and AI availability, then a weighted
scoring engine computes a 0-100 health score and a continuous-improvement
trend using real historical data, never invented numbers. A panorama module
cross-checks every node's inventory to catch duplicated or diverging systems
across the mesh before they become failures. We built this to answer NASA's
Lunar or Martian Outpost challenge: the same tradeoff logic that keeps our own
four-node Tailscale mesh healthy is the backbone a resource-management tool
for a lunar or Martian outpost needs — except instead of guessing, it is
grounded in real NASA space-weather data (NASA DONKI) to score radiation
risk. ACHE is Spanish for the cooperative's roots in La Cruz, Guanacaste,
Costa Rica, built by COOPECRUCEÑOS R.L. as living, working infrastructure —
not a mockup.
details:
WHAT IT DOES / HOW IT WORKS

ACHE (OMEGA) is a distributed mesh of 4 nodes connected over a private

Tailscale network, each running lightweight Python probes:

- ache_sonda_equipo.py: measures real hardware state per node (RAM, disk,

local AI/Ollama availability).

- ache_inventario.py / ache_panorama_merge.py: cross-node inventory with

duplicate and divergence detection, filtered to ACHE-relevant systems only.

- ache_salud_nodo.py: a weighted health-scoring model (RAM 25%, disk 15%,

network coverage 20%, sync 20%, local AI 10%, network quality 10%) that

renormalizes weights when data is missing rather than inventing values,

classifies each node OPTIMAL/GOOD/WARNING/CRITICAL, and computes a

continuous-improvement trend via linear regression over historical runs.

- ache_territorio.py: models each registered device's "ambito" (TERRA, LUNA,

MARTE, ORBITA) — the same field/tradeoff structure a lunar or Martian

outpost resource manager needs.

- ache_nasa_donki.py (new, v1.1.0): pulls REAL, LIVE NASA DONKI space-weather

data (solar flare class, via ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/DONKI-API) to compute a

BAJO/MEDIO/ALTO radiation-risk level for any device registered under LUNA,

MARTE, or ORBITA. Verified live on 2026-11-15: returned a real NASA flare

reading (class C2.8, risk level BAJO) — this is the real NASA data tying

our infrastructure directly to the Lunar/Martian Outpost challenge.

- A public Tailscale Funnel endpoint exposes the mesh's live status to the

outside world without any login.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

A real, working, self-monitoring cooperative node network that already runs

24/7 for COOPECRUCEÑOS R.L. in La Cruz, Guanacaste. The same health/tradeoff

mathematics that keeps 4 real machines coordinated is the exact mechanic a

lunar or Martian habitat's life-support/power/shielding management needs,

now connected to one real NASA data source instead of placeholder numbers.

TOOLS / LANGUAGES / HARDWARE / SOFTWARE

Python 3, PowerShell (orchestration via WinRM), Tailscale (mesh networking +

Funnel public exposure), 4 physical/virtual Windows nodes, NASA DONKI API

(ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/DONKI-API).

CREATIVITY

We did not build a game mockup — we adapted a working production system

(a cooperative's real IT mesh) into the exact resource-tradeoff structure

NASA's challenge describes, grounded in real space-weather data.

FACTORS CONSIDERED

Reliability (never fabricate a metric when data is missing), honesty about

current limitations (network-quality scoring not yet automated; some nodes

intermittently offline), and real-world validation (every module ships with

an automated self-test, not just a demo).

AI DISCLOSURE: Claude (Anthropic) was used throughout development to

accelerate coding, debugging, and documentation — writing and fixing Python/

PowerShell scripts, designing the health-scoring model's formulas, and

drafting this submission text. The core idea (a cooperative's real

infrastructure-monitoring mesh re-purposed for NASA's Lunar/Martian Outpost

resource-tradeoff challenge) originated with the team (Cristhian Andrés

Gonzaga Martínez, COOPECRUCEÑOS R.L.), not the AI. No AI-generated images,

video, or audio are included in this submission. Code assistance is

disclosed here per Space Apps rules.
